correctness.rationale: For any slice containing \(x\), active coordinates with \(|x_i|>R-1\) must have aligned functional coefficients, and the slice slack plus the one-coordinate obstruction yields \(a_i(R+1-|x_i|)\ge\delta\). Summing gives the necessary condition \(\Phi_x(R)\le1\). Conversely, for feasible r the active set is finite and weights proportional to \((r+1-|x_i|)^{-1}\), with leftover mass placed in the tail, define a norm-one slice functional whose radius approaches r. This gives the exact infimum formula. The statement that a remote zero coordinate gives the universal lower floor \(R\ge1\) is slightly over-literal for infinite-support x; the same step is valid by choosing tail coordinates with \(x_k\to0\), changing one to the opposite unit sign, and taking the supremum. No theorem statement changes. Fresh checks reproduced \((3+\sqrt{33})/8\) and the \(1/i\) threshold \(5/4\).
residual_risks: The proof sentence saying 'remote zero coordinate' should be read as the tail-limit argument for general infinite-support x; the correction is non-substantive and does not alter the formula.
The theorem is for real c0 only.

originality.rationale: Choi and Jung give lower bounds on the \(\Delta\)-constant in \(c_0\) and an exact equal-coordinate finite-support family, but their full primary text does not give an all-point coordinate formula. A current published theorem gives an exact formula on every real \(C(K)\) space and, when applied in \(c=C(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\})\) to the extension \(x\mapsto(x,0)\), produces the same numerical expression. This is a serious neighboring result but does not imply the c0 theorem: pointwise slice constants are ambient-space dependent, and an isometric embedding/codimension-one inclusion does not transfer the reverse inequality. Restricting ambient slices only yields the easy one-sided comparison; the assigned \(\ell_1\)-dual tail construction proves the missing c0-specific direction. No prior direct all-c0 formula was located.
